hero_card.label: Network coursework
hero_card.intro: Construct a network security project solution based on architectural components, traffic evidence, security controls, and risk decisions.

topics.title: Network Security Assignment Topics
topics.intro: Network security homework include a mixture of architecture, protocols and defensive controls. The best answers do not simply present each of these technologies as a definition, but rather explain how these elements operate as a whole.

problems.title: Network Security Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: Students regularly lose marks if diagrams, packet evidence or firewall selections are displayed without explaining the security purpose in network security coursework help.

workflow.title: Network Security Assignment Workflow

tools_report.title: Network Security Lab Tools
tools_report.intro: Use network tools to answer a specific question: what traffic is present, where a control applies, or what evidence supports the security conclusion.

long_copy.title: Network Security Report Writing Help
paragraphs: The architecture should be easy to understand before the discussion of individual controls in a network security report. Begin with key assets, users, network segments and trust boundaries, and describe the traffic flow expected to occur between them. A labelled diagram will be helpful when the text includes for the reference and explains the significance of each boundary.

Capture packets and screenshots of configurations must be selective. A Wireshark frame, report and output of firewall rule or a router supports the evidence if it is explained, why it is relevant and how it contributes to the security judgement. No interpretation means no weight for output.

The recommendation should directly follow the identified risks. When the report provides a description of the asset affected, threat, benefit, and any operations trade-offs, then segmentation, secure remote access, monitoring, access control and firewall changes become strong recommendations.

faq.title: Network Security Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Answers to common questions about network diagrams, packet evidence, firewalls, VPNs and security reporting.

signature.title: Network Security Control Map
signature.intro: Use this chain to connect the network design to the security argument in the report.

Describe the traffic path, weakness or trust relationship that creates security risk.

hero_card.label: Authorised lab work
hero_card.intro: Design scope, methodology, evidence, risk and responsible remediation-based ethics hacking coursework.

problems.title: Ethical Hacking Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: Running a tool is not a challenge, the hard part is usually showing why the test was appropriate, what the evidence proves and how the finding should be remediated in ethical hacking coursework help.

workflow.title: Ethical Hacking Assessment Workflow
workflow.intro: Keep the assignment aligned with scope and permission from the first step through evidence collection, risk analysis and final reporting.

topics.title: Ethical Hacking Lab Topics
topics.intro: Coursework may combine methodology, reconnaissance concepts, vulnerability assessment, web security, password security and professional reporting.

tools_report.title: Ethical Hacking Lab Tools
tools_report.intro: Tools such as Kali Linux utilities should appear in the report only when their output supports an authorised coursework objective.

long_copy.title: Ethical Hacking Report Writing Help
paragraphs: The report on ethical hacking or cyber security should start with scope and authorisation. Describe the environment under which the test is approved, what it was designed to test and any significant restrictions. This provides a clear academic and ethical context to the technical evidence.

Findings should be written in a consistent manner. State what component is compromised, describe the weakness observed, provide succinct evidence, articulate the impact to security and explain the risk rating. Screenshots should be used to back up the explanation, not as a substitute for it.

The remediation section is the part of a technical test where it turns into defensive security analysis. Recommendations should be tied to the cause of the risk and should describe how patching, configuration changes, access control changes, secure configuration or monitoring would mitigate the risk identified.

faq.title: Ethical Hacking Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Practical answers about authorised labs, Kali Linux evidence, vulnerability reports and remediation.

related.title: Related Ethical Hacking Subjects
related.intro: Ethical hacking commonly overlaps with penetration testing, web application security, network security and digital forensics.

cta.title: Ethical Hacking Assignment Help
cta.intro: Share the authorised lab brief, assessment criteria, deadline and any evidence you need to explain.

signature.title: Ethical Hacking Finding Anatomy
signature.intro: A good ethical hacking finding reads like a small evidence-led security argument.
items: State which approved system or lab component the finding relates to.
Present concise evidence and explain exactly what it demonstrates.
Connect the observation to a realistic consequence and justify severity.
Recommend a defensive change that addresses the root cause and can be verified.

hero_card.label: Forensic evidence

bullets: Evidence integrity and chain of custody

workflow.title: Digital Forensics Investigation Workflow
workflow.intro: In Forensic investigation workflow, evidence handling, examination, interpretation and reporting should be broken down into distinct stages within digital forensics coursework help.

problems.title: Digital Forensics Evidence Challenges
problems.intro: Good forensic evidence practice highlights actual evidence from what the student infers from the evidence about the event or evidence about the use of the evidence.

topics.title: Digital Forensics Assignment Topics
topics.intro: These are typically things such as evidence preservation, file system artefacts, timelines, logs, browser activities, metadata and forensic reporting.

tools_report.title: Digital Forensics Lab Tools
tools_report.intro: Examination should be reproducible using forensic tools. Write down the source that was studied, the artefact that was recognised and how the integrity was preserved.

long_copy.title: Digital Forensics Report Writing Help
paragraphs: Evidence should be separated from interpretation in a forensic report. Observations are items in the file metadata, log entries, browser records or times, but the explanation of what those records mean should be part of the analysis. Separating the two allows for easier conclusions to be made for digital forensics lab report help.

Special attention should be given to timelines. Identify each of the time-stamps; do not report events with uncertainty as proven facts when time zone or clock issues are involved. The most helpful timeline entries are those that alter the knowledge about the case.

The conclusion should be appropriate to the evidence provided. Summarise the most solidly supported findings and outline important limitations but refrain from claims that cannot be linked to an artefact, log, image or documented examination step.

faq.title: Digital Forensics Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Questions about chain of custody, forensic timelines, artefact interpretation and evidence-based conclusions.

related.title: Related Digital Forensics Subjects
related.intro: Digital forensics naturally links with incident response, malware analysis, threat intelligence and network security.

cta.title: Digital Forensics Assignment Help
cta.intro: Share the case scenario, evidence requirements, marking rubric and deadline for a focused review.

signature.title: From Evidence to Conclusion
signature.intro: All conclusions follow a visible reasoning chain in forensic reports, making it easier to defend them.
items: Document the source of the artefact and how integrity was ensured.
Determine which file, log, metadata, and/or timestamp/activity can be verified.
Describe the implications it implies, making a distinction between fact and inference.
State the conclusion that can reasonably be drawn from the available evidence.

topics.intro: Common university tasks include scope, reconnaissance ideas, vulnerability checking, evidence, risk ratings, remediation and professional reporting.

tools_report.title: Penetration Testing Lab Tools
tools_report.intro: Only use testing tools in the approved environment and record the evidence supporting each finding for authorised penetration testing lab help.

long_copy.title: Penetration Testing Report Writing Help
paragraphs: A scope of the penetration test should be displayed prior to any findings. Explain the authorisation, the exclusions, assumptions and rules of engagement to enable the reader to comprehend the nature of the evidence.

The pattern for each finding should be the same: Affected asset, observed condition, evidence, security impact, risk rating and remediation. This format facilitates comparison of findings and allows the assessor to observe the relationship between the technical observations and the professional judgements.

Remediation should be actionable. Explain why the weakness is the root cause, identify the control or configuration change and explain its priority and describe how the organisation could confirm the weakness is reduced after the control or configuration change had been implemented.

faq.title: Penetration Testing Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Answers about scope, findings, risk ratings, authorised testing and remediation reports.

related.title: Related Penetration Testing Subjects
related.intro: Often penetration testing is related to ethical hacking, web application security, network security and cryptography.

cta.title: Penetration Testing Assignment Help
cta.intro: Share the approved lab scope, assignment brief, marking rubric and deadline.

signature.title: Penetration Test Finding Anatomy
signature.intro: Ensure that the structure is the same for all of the technical observations so that each becomes a professional assessment finding for penetration testing lab report help.
items: The name of the authorised target/service should be clear and succinct enough for the reader to find the problem.
Demonstrate the least amount of evidence needed to prove the observed weakness.
Use the same likelihood and impact rating in the report.
Solve the cause, prioritize and confirm how to fix it.

hero_card.label: Cryptographic concepts
hero_card.intro: Describe encryption, hashing, PKI and key management and relate each to an authentic security need.

topics.title: Cryptography Assignment Concepts
topics.intro: Typical coursework on cryptography requires students to compare techniques, describe the security properties and explain why a certain technique is appropriate for a situation for applied cryptography assignment help.

problems.title: Cryptography Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: A frequent missing element is to adequately define an algorithm without providing an explanation of why it is suitable to the requirement or what constraints it places on the requirement.

workflow.title: Cryptography Assignment Workflow
workflow.intro: Solve from security requirement to cryptographic property, discuss appropriate approaches, explain implementation and key management decisions.

tools_report.title: Cryptography Tools and Examples
tools_report.intro: There should be practical examples to illustrate a concept, e.g., encryption, hashing, certificate validation and key handling, but not in place of the academic explanation.

long_copy.title: Cryptography Report Writing Help
paragraphs: Cryptography assignments are better if they start with the security requirement and then proceed to the algorithm name. Before considering appropriate methods determine if the task requires confidentiality, integrity, authentication, non-repudiation or a combination of these for applied cryptography coursework help.

Useful criteria for comparison – key distribution, performance, security assumptions, maturity, implementation context. No answer is required to choose one method or the other as "the best" answers to different problems; a good answer will identify points of symmetry and points of asymmetry, or the domains for their application.

Key management is a topic in its own right. Whether a cryptographic design is secure in practice can be determined by its use of generation, storage, distribution, rotation, backup and revocation. So a strong recommendation takes into account the algorithm as well as the lifecycle of the algorithm's keys.

faq.title: Cryptography Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Questions about encryption, hashing, PKI, digital signatures and key management.

related.title: Related Cryptography Subjects
related.intro: The applications of cryptography can be used in network security, cloud security, web application security, and secure authentication.

cta.title: Cryptography Assignment Help
cta.intro: Share the cryptography question, required algorithms or scenario, marking criteria and deadline.

signature.title: Encryption, Hashing and Signatures
signature.intro: The methods address distinct security issues and a cryptography assignment should also describe the property required before selecting a method.
items: Secure readable information with a key and who should be allowed to decrypted the information.
Produce a one way digest for verification purposes, explain why hashing is not encryption.
Include integrity and signer verification via private/public-key operations.
Describe the uses of certificates and chains of certificates to tie identities to public keys.

case_study.title: End to End Encryption and Digital Signature Analysis
case_study.intro: The Double Ratchet Algorithm is used for end to end encryption in apps such as Signal, WhatsApp, and Facebook Messenger.The key idea here is pretty straightforward: Each and every message has its very own key. It does this, by using two ratchets.

hero_card.intro: Distinguish static and dynamic evidence, and make defensive conclusions from lab observations.

problems.title: Malware Analysis Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: When writing about malware, care must be taken with the wording, as the report needs to differentiate between observation of a behavior and an assumption about a capability or intent within malware analysis coursework help.

topics.title: Malware Analysis Assignment Topics
topics.intro: Common areas are file properties, strings, hashes, process behaviour, persistence artefacts, network observations, indicators and defensive response.

workflow.title: Malware Analysis Lab Workflow
workflow.intro: Ensure the investigation remains within the scope of the authorised sandbox or University environment and evidence is captured in a repeatable sequence.

tools_report.title: Malware Analysis Lab Tools
tools_report.intro: Observe safely, document changes and collect defensive evidence using tools without going beyond the scope of the laboratory for malware analysis lab report help.

long_copy.title: Malware Analysis Report Writing Help
paragraphs: A malware analysis should be split into static and behavioural observations. Hashes, metadata and strings describe the sample prior to its execution, while processes, file changes, registry access or network events describe the activity that occurred in the safe lab environment.

It is a good idea to present indicators with context. The domain, file path or hash might be helpful to the detection, but the report should include information on the reliability of the indicator, what the indicator is, and if defenders would need additional context to avoid false positives.

Defensive recommendations should be derived from observed behaviour. Having a report that details which behaviour or artefact each recommendation covers is more convincing for monitoring, containment, endpoint controls and access restrictions, and for incident response actions.

faq.title: Malware Analysis Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Questions about safe analysis, static and dynamic evidence, indicators and defensive reporting.

related.title: Related Malware Analysis Subjects
related.intro: Malware analysis often connects with digital forensics, incident response, threat intelligence and network monitoring.

cta.title: Malware Analysis Assignment Help
cta.intro: Share the safe lab brief, evidence requirements, marking rubric and deadline.

signature.title: Static vs Behavioural Malware Analysis
signature.intro: The report should present how pre-execution artefacts and observations of the safe runtime complement each other for static and dynamic malware analysis coursework help.
items: View hashes, metadata, strings and file properties without executing the sample.
Monitor processes, files, registry and network inside the safe lab.
Make a judgement about likely behaviour after making several observations.
Identify and link to detection, containment or monitoring indicators.

hero_card.label: Cloud Security
hero_card.intro: Share the cloud risk concept of shared responsibility, identity, logging, data protection and platform-specific controls.

topics.title: Cloud Security Assignment Topics
topics.intro: The shared responsibility, IAM, storage security, encryption, logging, network controls, and monitoring and misconfiguration risk are all core topics.

problems.title: Cloud Security Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: Answering questions about cloud assignments can feel more generic unless the answer includes some of the service model attributes, assets, identities and/or configuration decisions that increase or decrease the risk.

workflow.title: Cloud Security Assignment Workflow
workflow.intro: Use the cloud service and cloud responsibility boundary as starting point, then assign threats to evidence, controls and risk based recommendations.

tools_report.title: Cloud Security Tools and Platforms
tools_report.intro: Platform screenshots and logs should prove a configuration or event and be followed by an explanation of its security significance.

long_copy.title: Cloud Security Report Writing Help
paragraphs: Cloud security reports should clearly state the service model. The roles and responsibilities for the security of infrastructure, platform services and software services are different, so the report should detail which security controls are the provider's responsibility and which are the customer's.

The analysis may focus on identity, and it is common for identity to be at the core of the analysis. Roles, policies, MFA and permissions should be assessed using the principle of least privilege and business need. A good screenshot of an IAM policy can only be useful when the text that accompanies it clarifies what access it's giving and why it is necessary or not.

Platform awareness should be a part of cloud recommendations. Logging, encryption, network restrictions, secure storage, backup and monitoring controls are more robust if they refer to the specific risk and how the proposed change would enhance visibility or minimise exposure.

faq.title: Cloud Computing Assignment Rubric
faq.intro: The rubrics typically found in cloud computing assignments favor clarity around the cloud service model, the security issues to address, quality of evidence, IAM determinations, and practical platform-specific suggestions.

related.title: Related Cloud Security Subjects
related.intro: The areas of cloud security often intersect with network security, cryptography, incident response and web application security.

cta.title: Cloud Security Assignment Help
cta.intro: Know and understand the cloud security models, identity controls, logging, storage protection and risk analysis, and discuss how each of these relates to the cloud service, threat, and assignment scenarios.

signature.title: Cloud Shared Responsibility Map
signature.intro: A cloud-security solution should demonstrate the control of each layer before security recommendations are made.
items: Discuss the security duties that the platform provider continues to assume.
Determine permissions, data, settings and workloads that the customer needs to obtain.
Make sure to present evidence from platforms to demonstrate effective handling of responsibility.
Propose a solution to the gap, such as the IAM, logging, encryption or network change.

hero_card.label: Web Application Security
hero_card.intro: Relate OWASP risks and authorised evidence to make design, coding and remediation choices.

topics.title: Web Application Security Topics
topics.intro: Classes include topics like OWASP risks, authentication, access control, input handling, session security, secure coding and remediation.

problems.title: Web Security Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: Students may conclude that a weakness is correct, but they lose marks because they don't tie the weakness to the feature that it is affecting, security impact and appropriate defensive control.

workflow.title: Web Security Assignment Workflow
workflow.intro: Interpret authorised lab evidence in relation to the use and interpretation of the application scenario in terms of what is allowed and what is required.

tools_report.title: Web Security Lab Tools
tools_report.intro: A defensive coursework objective should be supported using a tool such as OWASP ZAP or Burp Suite within an authorised training environment.

long_copy.title: Web Security Report Writing Help
paragraphs: The report of a web security incident should be preceded by a description of the feature of the application that is being compromised, rather than naming a vulnerability category. State why the feature was designed to perform the operation, explain the security assumption that was violated, and describe what evidence shows the security assumption is broken in the authorised environment.

OWASP categories are useful for classification purposes but should not be the substitute for analysis. The report should also cover why the chosen remediation will deal with the root cause or underlying matter, and the relevant security principle that would be affected.

Remediation should tie in code, configuration and architecture. Each of these areas is solving a different problem and recommendations should be specific to the condition observed and have a means to confirm the change.

faq.title: Web Security Assignment Questions
faq.intro: The student should be aware of the vulnerability of the application and the security measure used to prevent the vulnerability in the web security reports.

related.title: Related Web Security Subjects
related.intro: Web application security is related to ethical hacking, penetration testing, cryptography and cloud security.

cta.title: Web Application Security Assignment Help
cta.intro: Understand how risks to web applications can be identified, demonstrated and explained in authorised coursework, focusing on secure design, OWASP principles, risk interpretation and remediation in practice.

signature.title: OWASP Finding to Secure Fix
signature.intro: Explain the application-specific weakness and defensive design change with OWASP categories as context.
items: Specify the login, form, API, access-control check, etc., feature of the application.
Describe how the failed validation, authentication, session or configuration principle is supposed to work.
Relate weakness to impacted data, users or business processes.
Suggest code, configuration or architecture control remedying the root cause.

hero_card.label: Cyber Threat Intelligence
hero_card.intro: Develop defensible intelligence judgements and defensible priorities from turn sources, indicators and behavioural evidence.

problems.title: Threat Intelligence Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: The hard part of CTI is not gathering information, it's determining what is reliable, what the evidence has determined and what the defenders should do with the judgement.

topics.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Topics
topics.intro: The course typically includes the topics of intelligence requirements, source evaluation, threat actors, indicators, TTPs, MITRE ATT&CK and defensive implications.

workflow.title: Threat Intelligence Assignment Workflow
workflow.intro: Set the intelligence requirement first, then gather, analyze, process and disseminate only the information required to meet that requirement.

tools_report.title: Threat Intelligence Tools
tools_report.intro: There is a strong need to enhance the provenance and analysis of platforms and public sources instead of allowing these to become a list of indicators.

long_copy.title: Threat Intelligence Report Writing Help
paragraphs: The intelligence requirement is the starting point for a threat intelligence report. Specify the audience, decision and time frame for the research to have a clear purpose. This helps to avoid the report being a disjointed series of threat details.

It should be clear in the reasoning why the sources have been chosen. Consider reliability, recency, corroboration and whether the source had direct access to the information. Indicators or reported behaviour should then be distinguished from analytical judgement.

Key judgement, confidence and defensive implication should be stated as the conclusion. The value of MITRE ATT&CK mappings, indicators and threat-actor context is limited unless its use aids and assists the reader in determining what to monitor, prioritize, or harden.

faq.title: Threat Intelligence Assignment Questions
faq.intro: The typical way to earn CTI rewards is to provide well-structured thinking, not necessarily a lot of indicators or threat reports.

related.title: Related Threat Intelligence Subjects
related.intro: Threat intelligence is an overlap of incident response, malware analysis, digital forensics and network defence.

cta.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Assignment Help
cta.intro: Learn how to utilize security data and open sources to create valuable intelligence using different methods including assessing sources, distinguishing indicators from conclusions, and mapping the behavior and communicating the next steps for defenders.

signature.title: Source to Defensive Action
signature.intro: Threat intelligence is effective when the journey from the raw source to a security decision is clear.
items: Verify the recency, access, corroboration and possible bias of a claim.
Distinguish indicators and reported behaviour from assumptions or attributions.
State the conclusion, backing up evidence, uncertainty and level of confidence.
Convert judgement to monitoring, prioritisation, detection or hardening decisions.

hero_card.label: Cloud architecture coursework
hero_card.intro: Identify, create and describe cloud solutions based on service and deployment models, virtualisation, scalable architecture and platform evidence.

topics.title: Cloud Computing Assignment Topics
topics.intro: Cloud Computing assignments frequently delve into service design, platform choices, virtualisation, scalability, and real-world implementation choices.

problems.title: Cloud Computing Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: However, most often, the biggest hurdle is translating general cloud jargon into an appropriate architecture that aligns with the scenario and marking rubric.

workflow.title: Cloud Computing Assignment Workflow
workflow.intro: A good cloud workflow begins with the workload and requirements and then moves to picking a suitable service model and designing the architecture; it then evaluates the scalability, availability, and platform options.

tools_report.title: Cloud Computing Tools and Platforms
tools_report.intro: Include architecture diagrams and AWS/Azure images to show the concept of cloud, not unrelated screenshots of platforms in the report.

long_copy.title: Cloud Computing Report Writing Help
paragraphs: Before recommending a platform or service, a cloud computing report should state the workload and requirements. Describe the users, data, performance requirements, expected scale and availability requirements in order to evaluate architecture options to a problem for cloud architecture assignment help.

The responsibility and control are the aspects that should be compared to service models. IaaS provides increased infrastructure management, PaaS provides decreased platform management and SaaS provides a full application service. The strongest comparison will give the explanation of which model is the best for the given scenario, and why.

The written analysis should be supplemented with architecture diagrams. Compute, storage, networking, databases and scaling elements should be clearly named and the report should explain how those elements operate together to ensure cloud operations are manageable and provide availability and performance.

faq.title: Cloud Computing Assignment FAQs
faq.intro: Answers about service models, cloud architecture, AWS, Azure, virtualisation and assignment rubrics.

related.title: Related Cloud Computing Subjects
related.intro: Cloud computing is closely related with cloud security, information security, network security and web application security.

cta.title: Cloud Computing Assignment Help
cta.intro: Share the cloud computing brief, marking rubric, platform requirements and deadline for a focused review.

signature.title: Cloud Model to Architecture Map
signature.intro: Follow this sequence to transform an idea for cloud computing into a valid technical design.
items: Before selecting cloud services, it is important to define a user, define data, scale, performance and availability.
Choose IaaS, PaaS or SaaS based on the level of control and management in the scenario.
Match compute, storage, networking and data services with the compute workload.
Make sense of scalability, availability, cost/management considerations and defend architecture.

hero_card.label: Information Security
hero_card.intro: Link information assets, CIA requirements, risk, policies, and governance and controls in a single security analysis based on evidence.

topics.title: Information Security Assignment Topics
topics.intro: Courses typically include a mix of information security topics such as risk management, CIA triad, policy, access control, governance, and continuity and control selection.

problems.title: Information Security Coursework Challenges
problems.intro: Students may be able to describe a security concept properly but are unable to link the concepts to the assets, risks and business requirements described in the scenario and thus lose marks.

workflow.title: Information Security Assignment Workflow
workflow.intro: A robust workflow will be able to recognize information assets, understand the threats and vulnerabilities, and determine the risk; and then justify why policies and controls are required to address the risk.

tools_report.title: Information Security Tools and Frameworks
tools_report.intro: The analysis should be provided with the help of the risk matrices, asset registers, policy templates and recognised security frameworks, but not be constrained by them.

long_copy.title: Information Security Report Writing Help
paragraphs: The information or business process that needs protection is the first thing that should be included in an information security report. Once assets have been identified it is easier to explain why confidentiality, integrity or availability is important, and what the consequences of a security failure would be.

Risk analysis should demonstrate that threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact and controls are correlated and can be traced. A risk score is of no value if the report doesn't indicate how it's calculated and why one risk is considered more or less important than another.

Policies and controls should be commensurate with the identified risk. Administrative controls are responsibilities and expectations, technical controls are security means by which they are enforced or monitored, and physical controls protect facilities and equipment. Strong Recommendations describe the interaction of these layers.

faq.title: Information Security Assignment Questions
faq.intro: Information security solutions are more robust when presented in the context of a real organisation or scenario, rather than a set of terms defined separately.

related.title: Related Information Security Subjects
related.intro: Information security provides a foundation for network security, cloud security, cryptography and cyber threat intelligence.

cta.title: Information Security Assignment Help
cta.intro: Develop information security assignments related to assets, threats, vulnerabilities, risk and controls; relate confidentiality, integrity and availability to information security policies, governance and business needs.

signature.title: Information Asset to Security Control
signature.intro: Follow this sequence to link business information to a sound security recommendation.
items: State the information, system/business process and describe its purpose.
Indicate one or more of the properties of confidentiality, integrity, availability as most important.
Describe what might go wrong, what is the weakness that would allow it to happen, and the possible consequences.
Propose a suitable administrative, technical or physical control that is proportionate to the risk and describe the risk reduction anticipated.
